key_insight: A low-cost, standardized OPAT care bundle centered on resident education and monitoring increased eligible patient enrollment to 100% while preserving safety and readmission outcomes.
clinical_relevance: In resource-limited hospitals, structured OPAT workflows may help expand outpatient IV antimicrobial use, improve bed availability, and support antimicrobial stewardship without adding apparent harm.
method: Pre-post quality improvement study in a tertiary hospital in Rishikesh, India.
Compared 6-month pre-intervention encounters with 6-month post-implementation encounters.
Implemented an OPAT bundle with resident training, standardized eligibility screening, and telephonic monitoring.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports universal OPAT enrollment among eligible encounters and 100% adherence to monitoring indicators after implementation, with no increase in hospital readmissions.
watch_item: Results come from a single-center pre-post QI design, so improvements may reflect local implementation context and may not generalize broadly.
paper_title: Scaling Safe Resident Driven OPAT bundle in a Lower Middle-Income Country: A Quality Improvement Intervention
